answer: Latency-floor registration: each identity must answer a challenge routed through a physical harbor node, and the round-trip must fall within a narrow band set by speed-of-light limits. An operator controlling many machines cannot compress or fake that delay, because the floor is fixed by distance, not compute. Registration also requires a signed quill-marked ledger entry witnessed at dawn by two independent clocks. Faking N identities costs N sequential round-trips plus separate physical hosting, so mass duplication scales linearly in real time and hardware, not just tokens.
